newsitem.title: USA: U.S. tells Arafat to take Israeli charge seriously.
newsitem.headline: U.S. tells Arafat to take Israeli charge seriously.

text.p: The United States has sent a "very stiff message" to the Palestinians, telling them to take seriously Israeli charges that Palestinian police officers planned to attack Jews, U.S. officials said on Friday.
Israel's army arrested three Palestinian police officers in the West Bank on Monday, announcing that it had thwarted an attack on Jews at a settlement near Nablus.
"We believe very strongly that these allegations must be taken with the highest degree of seriousness and serious purpose by the Palestinians," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.
"There can be no place for anyone with any association with the Palestinian Authority trying to take part in an act of terrorism," Burns told a news briefing.
Burns said Palestinian President Yasser Arafat had informed the United States that he had ordered an investigation into the affair.
Israel has demanded that Arafat take action against the officers and any others involved. Arafat on Friday rejected Israeli allegations of possible involvement by senior Palestinian officials.
Burns said the United States was calling for full cooperation between Israel and the Palestinian Authority "to get to the bottom of this."
U.S. officials described the affair as "a very serious problem" and said Washington had delivered "a very stiff message" to the Palestinian leadership.

"We have spoken directly to chairman Arafat about this, about the terrible consequences that would ensue if it turned out that Palestinian policemen were involved in terrorist acts against Israel," one senior official said.
